# dnsman: registrant contact as portal-managed config (per-group, house fallback)

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-07-30
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Project**: django-mojo
- **Pairs with**: board item **952** (web-mojo — the Registrant Contact admin page). 952 depends on this item; build this one first.

Apply rules: `django-mojo-build-conventions`, `nativemojo-board-conventions`.

## Description

Domain purchasing refuses at quote time until a registrant contact is configured, and today the only way to configure one is `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` in the deployment's server settings. It should be manageable from the dnsman admin portal instead.

This is the **backend half**: make the registrant contact a DB-backed, per-group setting with a house (global) fallback, and expose read/write REST so the portal can render and save a form.

## Context

`registrar._registrant_contact()` reads `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` and raises when it is missing or incomplete. `quote()` calls it as a preflight before any AWS call; `purchase()` reads it again for the real registration. `GET /api/dnsman/config` reports only a `registrant_contact_configured` boolean, because the contact is PII and is deliberately never echoed. Net effect: an operator sees "purchasing is unavailable" with no way to fix it short of a deploy.

The plumbing for this already exists. `Setting` (`mojo/apps/account/models/setting.py`) is DB-backed with an optional `group` FK, and `settings.get(name, group=..., kind="dict")` resolves Redis cache → DB (group → parent chain → global) → `django.conf.settings`. A JSON string in `Setting.value` is parsed into a dict by the `kind="dict"` branch. So "group row overrides global row overrides the deploy's conf file" works with **no changes to the settings layer**.

## Decisions (confirmed with Ian, 2026-07-30)

- **Scope**: per-group, falling back to the house contact. A group with its own contact uses it; otherwise the global one.
- **Permission**: `manage_dns` (not `view_dns`).
- **Storage**: the existing `Setting` table under the current key `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT`. No new model, no migration.
- **Portal placement**: a new page under System → DNS (item 952).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `registrar._registrant_contact(group=None)` resolves per-group with global fallback; `quote()` passes its `group`, `purchase()` passes **`row.group`** (see D0).
- [ ] `GET /api/dnsman/config` reports `registrant_contact_configured` for the requested group (`?group=`) — the group's own row if present, else the house contact. Unchanged global answer when no group is supplied.
- [ ] New REST to **read** the contact for editing, gated on `manage_dns`.
- [ ] New REST to **write/clear** a contact for a scope, gated on `manage_dns`, validating the full ICANN required-field set before it persists — so a bad contact is a readable 400 at save time rather than an AWS bounce mid-purchase.
- [ ] A tenant admin (perms held only on a GroupMember row) can read and write **their group's** contact, and can never read the house contact's values. Global scope requires a platform admin (`rest/gates.py: require_platform_admin`).
- [ ] `view_dns` alone reads neither scope; the existing regression in `tests/test_dnsman/10_security_regressions.py` (view_dns must not reach registrant PII) stays green.
- [ ] The contact is never echoed into `GET /api/dnsman/config`, logs, or any REST graph.
- [ ] A contact saved via REST is picked up by the next quote with no restart.
- [ ] Deployments still setting `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` in the conf file keep working unchanged when no DB row exists.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_dnsman/` per the Testing plan below.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/django_developer/dnsman/Registrar.md`, `docs/django_developer/dnsman/README.md` settings table, `docs/web_developer/dnsman/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

# Plan

## Objective

`DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` becomes editable at runtime, per group, through two new dnsman REST endpoints — without ever exposing the operator's house contact to a tenant, and without a new model or migration. A group with its own contact registers domains under it; a group without one falls back to the house contact; a deployment that still sets the key in `django.conf` keeps working untouched.

## Design decisions

### D0 — `purchase()` resolves the contact from `row.group`, never its `group` argument

`purchase(group, user, purchase_id, token)` treats `group` as **optional attribution**, not authority: `registrar.py:580-584` only compares it when non-None ("passing none adopts the quote's own group"), and the Domain is created with `group=row.group` (:599). `request.group` is `Group.get_active(...)`, which returns `None` for a deactivated or typo'd id (`http.py:101`) — reachable over REST because `requires_params("group")` is satisfied by `request.DATA`, not by successful resolution.

So resolving the contact from the argument would file the **house** contact on a tenant's domain whenever their group went inactive between quote and confirm — at the one irreversible, real-money step. The read must be `_registrant_contact(row.group)`, inside the existing `select_for_update` block, so quote-time validation and redemption resolve the same scope.

### D1 — Global scope is platform-admin; group scope is `manage_dns` on that group

`mojo/models/rest.py:_evaluate_permission` branches on whether `request.group` is set:

- **`?group=<id>` present** → `request.group.user_has_permission(request.user, perms, …)`.
- **no group** → `request.user.has_permission(perms)`, the caller's **global** permission dict.

The property this relies on is precise, and narrower than it first appears. `Group.user_has_permission` (`group.py:210-212`) **short-circuits on the user's global dict before consulting GroupMember**. So a holder of *global* `manage_dns`/`security` — or a superuser — reaches every group's contact by naming its id, without membership. That is pre-existing framework shape, shared by `quote()`, `purchase()` and every other dnsman endpoint; this item does not change it and must not claim to.

What genuinely holds, and is what this design needs: a **tenant admin** holds `manage_dns` on a GroupMember row, not on the User, so they cannot reach the no-group branch and cannot reach another tenant's group. The house contact stays invisible to them.

On top of the model check, the global scope calls `require_platform_admin(request, "Managing the house registrant contact")` — the house contact is the operator's own personal data and is the registrant of record for every tenant without one, so it takes the same gate as the other house-account operations in `gates.py`, which also refuses key-backed sessions.

Group-scoped ApiKeys may write their own group's contact — ordinary tenant DNS authority, bounded by `is_group_allowed`.

### D2 — Store it as `is_secret=True`, validate in the service layer

`Setting.register_validator()` and `is_secret` are mutually exclusive (`setting.py:135-140` raises for a validated secret key), and `register_validator`'s `global_only=True` default would reject group rows outright. So this is a real either/or:

- **Plaintext + registered validator** puts the contact in `Setting.value`, which the generic settings REST (`Setting.RestMeta.VIEW_PERMS = ["manage_settings", "groups"]`) serializes as `display_value` (`setting.py:73-77`, in the default graph's `extra`). Every `manage_settings` holder could read the operator's home address off `/api/account/settings`. Worse than today.
- **`is_secret=True`** puts it in `mojo_secrets`, `display_value` returns `"******"`, and `serializer.py:185-212` appends `mojo_secrets` to `exclude_fields` unconditionally — including on the unknown-graph fallback, so `?graph=anything` cannot reach it either.

`is_secret` wins. Validation moves into `registrar.validate_contact()`, called by the write endpoint (readable 400) *and* by `_registrant_contact()` at read time (quote-time refusal, as today). A value written through the generic settings API bypasses the write check but still cannot reach AWS — `_registrant_contact()` refuses it before any spend. Fail-closed either way.

Round-trip verified end to end: `MojoSecrets.set_secret` stores the dict, `crypto.encrypt/decrypt` returns an objict, `get_value()` hands `kind="dict"` a dict it passes straight through, and the Redis path `json.dumps` → `objict.from_json` reproduces the original with `ExtraParams` lists intact.

**Do not overclaim in the docs.** `MojoSecrets._get_secrets_password` (`secrets.py:48-53`) derives the key from `f"{created}{pk}{ClassName}"` — all non-secret columns of the same row. This is REST masking, not meaningful encryption against someone holding the database. Say that plainly.

**Known, pre-existing:** `push_to_cache()` writes the *decrypted* value into Redis for secret settings — true of every secret setting today. Not introduced here, not fixed here.

### D3 — Do not pin the contact to a quote, but record which one was filed

`purchase()` re-reads the contact at redemption, so an edit between quote and confirm changes the registrant that gets filed. Pinning is still the wrong call: the quote TTL is 15 minutes, the price is unaffected, and refusing a redeemed-once quote over a benign edit is worse than accepting the more current contact.

But *not pinning* and *not recording* are different things, and the ledger must still be able to answer "whose contact was filed on this domain" once the answer is tenant-editable. `DomainPurchase.metadata` is an existing `JSONField` (`domain_purchase.py:78`) that the service already writes post-registration (`registrar.py:634-639`), and it appears in **neither** graph — `basic` and `default` both list fields explicitly (`domain_purchase.py:115-124`). So alongside `privacy_applied`, record:

- `registrant_scope` — the group id the contact resolved from, or `"house"`.
- `registrant_fingerprint` — a salted SHA-256 of the canonicalized contact.

No migration, no new PII surface, nothing refused. Document that a quote does not pin the contact and that the confirmation-time contact is the one filed.

### D4 — Validate shape, not just presence

Today `_registrant_contact()` only checks that required fields are non-empty, then hands the dict to `route53.register()`. Three ways that still fails **after** durable intent:

- `ContactType` outside the AWS enum. Verified against the installed botocore model (`route53domains/2014-05-15`): `PERSON`, `COMPANY`, `ASSOCIATION`, `PUBLIC_BODY`, `RESELLER`.
- `PhoneNumber` not in ICANN `+<cc>.<number>` form.
- **An unknown key → `ParamValidationError` from botocore before the call goes out.** A typo'd field name in a hand-written setting is silently accepted today and detonates at purchase time.

`validate_contact()` enforces: required fields present (plus `State` for US/CA); `ContactType` ∈ enum; `PhoneNumber` matches `^\+\d{1,3}\.\d{4,15}$`; `CountryCode` is two A–Z letters; every key is a member of the AWS `ContactDetail` shape (`FirstName`, `LastName`, `ContactType`, `OrganizationName`, `AddressLine1`, `AddressLine2`, `City`, `State`, `CountryCode`, `ZipCode`, `PhoneNumber`, `Email`, `Fax`, `ExtraParams` — the full list, so ccTLD deployments using `ExtraParams` keep working).

`CountryCode` is shape-checked only, not against the 251-entry enum: botocore does not enforce enums client-side, AWS rejects a bogus code, and the failure being guarded is malformed data, not an invented country.

Both existing fixtures (`4_registrar.py:25-36`, `12_config.py:72-78`) already satisfy the stricter rules, so no existing test goes red. **Migration note:** a deployment whose conf-file contact has a non-conforming phone number starts refusing quotes instead of failing at AWS — fail-closed, and visible (`registrant_contact_configured` reports `false` and the read endpoint names the field).

### D5 — Endpoint shape

`GET`/`POST` on one path, group selected by the framework's standard `?group=`, no dynamic segments (per `.claude/rules/rest.md`):

```
GET  /api/dnsman/registrant[?group=<id>]
POST /api/dnsman/registrant[?group=<id>]     body: {"contact": {...}} | {"clear": true}
```

Both return:

```json
{
  "scope": "global" | "group",
  "group": <id> | null,
  "contact": {...} | null,
  "source": "database" | "settings_file" | "none",
  "inherited": true,
  "effective_configured": true,
  "problems": []
}
```

- `contact`, `source` and `problems` describe **this scope's own row only**. For a group with no row: `contact: null`, `source: "none"`, `problems: []` — `problems` must never report on an inherited contact, or a tenant learns which fields of the house contact are malformed.
- `source` is only ever `database`/`none` for a group scope; `settings_file` is reachable only on the global scope, telling the operator that saving will create a DB row shadowing the file.
- `inherited` — group scope with no own row but a contact in effect above it.
- `effective_configured` — what `quote()` would decide for this scope right now; same answer as `GET /config`'s `registrant_contact_configured`.

### D6 — The scoped contact fills Registrant *and* Admin *and* Tech (confirmed with Ian, 2026-07-30)

`route53.register()` sends the same dict as all three (`route53.py:454-456`), on the house AWS account and the operator's payment method. With one house contact that is harmless. Once the contact is per-tenant it means a tenant `manage_dns` holder also sets the **admin and technical** contact of record — the addresses that receive transfer-approval and change-of-registrant mail — on an asset the operator owns and pays for.

**Ian chose to keep all three roles on the one scoped contact.** No code change: `route53.register()` and `purchase()` keep their current shape. The consequence is documentary and it is not optional — `Registrar.md:147-153` currently promises the opposite ("Domains are registered with the operator's contact as registrant of record and held on behalf of the tenant"), and that paragraph must be rewritten to state plainly that a tenant which sets its own contact holds registrant, admin **and** technical authority on that domain.

Also for the runbook, and inherent to the feature rather than to this choice: ICANN's 15-day verification rides the **registrant** email, so per-tenant contacts put that clock — and the domain-suspension risk behind it — on an address the operator does not monitor.

## Implementation steps

**Step 0 — baseline.** `bin/run_tests --agent`, read `var/test_failures.json`, record totals + any pre-existing failures under `## Notes`. Per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`, stop and report if the suite is already red.

**Step 1 — `mojo/apps/dnsman/services/registrar.py`: validation + scoped read/write.**
- Add `CONTACT_FIELDS` (the 14 AWS `ContactDetail` members), `CONTACT_TYPES`, `PHONE_RE`, beside `REQUIRED_CONTACT_FIELDS`/`STATE_REQUIRED_COUNTRIES` at :81-87.
- `validate_contact(contact)` → list of problem strings (empty = valid). Must keep naming missing fields — `4_registrar.py:604` asserts `"Email" in str(raised)`.
- `_registrant_contact(group=None)` reads `settings.get("DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT", {}, group=group, kind="dict")` and raises `me.ValueException` with the existing two message shapes, built from `validate_contact()`.
- `read_contact(group=None)` → `(own_contact, source)` for exactly that scope, no fallback: `Setting.objects.filter(key=KEY, group=group).first()` + `get_value()`, falling back to `django.conf` only for the global scope. `settings.get()` cannot express "this scope only".
- `save_contact(contact, group=None)` → validate, then `Setting.set(KEY, contact, is_secret=True, group=group)`.
- `clear_contact(group=None)` → `Setting.remove(KEY, group=group)`.

**Step 2 — call sites in the same file.** `quote()` :474 → `_registrant_contact(group)`. `purchase()` :589 → `_registrant_contact(row.group)` — **not** the `group` argument (D0). Write `registrant_scope` + `registrant_fingerprint` into the metadata dict already assembled at :634-639 (D3).

**Step 3 — `mojo/apps/dnsman/services/config.py`.** `_registrant_contact_configured(group=None)` and `get_config(group=None)`. Nothing else in `get_config()` becomes group-aware.

**Step 4 — `mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/config.py`.** Pass `request.group`. **Replace the docstring line claiming nothing here varies per group.**

**Step 5 — new `mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/registrant.py`.**
- `@md.GET('registrant')` and `@md.POST('registrant')`.
- **Order matters.** First mirror the group-resolution guard from `rest/purchase.py:132-135` — if `"group" in request.DATA or "group_uuid" in request.DATA` and `request.group is None`, raise a readable `ValueException`. This runs *before* `require_platform_admin` so a tenant whose group was just deactivated gets a 400 explaining it, instead of tripping the `not_superuser` branch that `gates.py` exists to alert on.
- Then: `request.group is None` → `require_platform_admin(request, "Managing the house registrant contact")`.
- Then `Domain.rest_check_permission_or_raise(request, ["SAVE_PERMS", "VIEW_PERMS"])` on both verbs — read is gated at write level on purpose because the payload is PII. Note `get_rest_meta_prop` returns the *first* non-None key, i.e. `SAVE_PERMS` = `["manage_dns", "security"]`; `view_dns` is genuinely excluded.
- POST reads `request.DATA` only; accepts `{"contact": {...}}` or `{"clear": true}`; returns the same body as GET.
- Add `from .registrant import *` to `mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/__init__.py`.

**Step 6 — docs + changelog.** No AWS-helper change: D6 resolved to one contact for all three roles, so `route53.register()` and `purchase()`'s call to it are untouched.

## Edge cases and error handling

- **Queryset deletes bypass cache eviction.** `Setting.objects.filter(...).delete()` does not run `Model.delete()`, so `remove_from_cache()` never fires and a stale Redis entry keeps resolving (no `pre_delete`/`post_delete` receivers exist for `Setting`). Every teardown and the `clear` path must go through `Setting.remove()` / instance `.delete()`.
- **`Setting.group` is `on_delete=CASCADE`** — deleting a Group cascades its Setting rows through the collector, same stale-Redis hole. Tests that delete groups must remove their settings first.
- **`?group=` on an inactive group** resolves to `None` and would silently become global scope; the Step 5 guard turns that into a readable 400.
- **`clear` on the global scope** when a conf-file value exists reverts to the file, not to "unconfigured". `source` reports `settings_file` afterwards.
- **Empty/whitespace-only values** count as missing — the existing `str(...).strip()` check stays.
- **`ExtraParams`** passes the key allow-list but is not shape-validated; AWS validates it. Document, do not build a form for it.
- **Parent-group inheritance.** `Setting.resolve()` walks the parent chain, so a child group inherits its parent's contact before falling back to global. Existing settings semantics and the desired behaviour; the read endpoint still shows only the group's own row, so a child reports `inherited: true` without revealing the parent's values.
- **PII in errors.** Problem strings name *fields*, never values. No contact value in any log line or exception message.

## Testing plan

New file `tests/test_dnsman/15_registrant.py`, reusing `tests/test_dnsman/_helpers.py` (`make_user`, `make_group_member`, `make_group`, `login`, `assert_no_secrets`, `DNS_PERMS`).

**Contamination control.** testit exposes no teardown decorator, so cleanup must happen in `@th.django_unit_setup()` — delete any `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` row **through `Setting.remove()`** for the global scope and every group used, before creating anything (`.claude/rules/testing.md`: setup cleans up before it creates). The at-risk neighbour is **`12_config.py:72` `test_config_no_pii_or_secrets`**, which sets the value via `th.server_settings` (the conf file) — a leaked global DB row shadows it. `4_registrar.py` is immune: its `_settings()` helper (:50-62) is `mock.patch.object(settings_obj, "get", …)` matching by name, which intercepts ahead of the DB. Files run in numeric order, so 12 precedes 15 and the real exposure is the *next* run after an interrupted one.

Cases:
1. Global write by a platform admin, then read back → `source: "database"`, contact echoed.
2. Group write by a member with `manage_dns` on that group, then read → the group's own contact.
3. **Fallback**: group with no row, house contact set → `contact: null`, `inherited: true`, `effective_configured: true`. Assert the house values appear **nowhere** in the body.
4. **Override**: group row set → `_registrant_contact(group)` returns the group's contact, not the house one.
5. Cross-tenant: a **GroupMember-only** admin of group A using `?group=<B>` → 403. (Documents the tenant-admin boundary — not a claim about global-perm holders; see D1.)
6. A global-perm holder (`make_user(DNS_PERMS)`) reaching another group by id **succeeds** — asserted deliberately so the pre-existing framework behaviour is recorded, not mistaken for isolation.
7. Tenant admin with no `?group=` → 403, and the house contact is not disclosed.
8. `view_dns` only → 403 on GET and POST.
9. Incomplete contact POST → 400 naming the missing fields; no row written.
10. Bad `ContactType` / malformed `PhoneNumber` / unknown key → 400 naming the field.
11. `?group=<deactivated id>` → 400 from the Step 5 guard, not a platform-admin 403.
12. `clear` removes the row *and* the Redis entry — assert by re-reading through `settings.get`, not by querying the DB.
13. Quote-time: incomplete group contact still refuses before any AWS call.
14. **D0 regression**: a quote taken for group X, then `purchase()` called with `group=None`, files X's contact — not the house one. Fails on the pre-fix code.
15. `GET /api/dnsman/config?group=<id>` reports the per-group boolean and still never echoes the contact (`assert_no_secrets`).

Existing tests that must stay green unedited: `4_registrar.py`, `12_config.py`, `10_security_regressions.py:215`, `9_tenant_isolation.py`.

Run `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_dnsman` while iterating, then the full default suite before closing. Never `--full` unless Ian asks.

## Documentation plan

- `docs/django_developer/dnsman/Registrar.md` — rewrite runbook step 1 (portal-managed, not a settings key); add the per-group/house fallback; add "a quote does not pin the contact, and the ledger records which scope was filed" (D3); **rewrite Custody (:147-153)** — it currently promises the operator is registrant of record, which stops being true; per D6 it must say a tenant with its own contact holds registrant, admin **and** technical authority on that domain; **extend the ICANN registrant-email verification warning** — per-tenant registrant emails mean per-tenant 15-day windows and a suspension risk the operator is not watching.

### Challenge

An independent red-team pass reviewed this plan against the code. Dispositions:

- **`purchase()` must use `row.group`, not its `group` argument** — *amended*. The strongest objection and a genuine money bug: `group` is optional attribution (`registrar.py:580-584`), `row.group` is authority (:599), and `request.group` is `None` for a deactivated id — so the original Step 2 would have filed the house contact on a tenant's domain at the irreversible step. Now D0, with regression test 14.
- **The contact is Admin and Tech, not just Registrant** — *amended*. Verified at `route53.py:454-456`. The workspec had excluded role-splitting as out of scope; making the contact per-tenant is what changes its meaning. Raised as D6 rather than decided silently; **Ian chose to keep all three roles on the one contact**, so the resolution is documentary — the Custody paragraph must stop claiming the operator is registrant of record.
- **D1's justification was factually wrong** — *amended*. `Group.user_has_permission` short-circuits on the user's global dict *before* GroupMember (`group.py:210-212`), so "naming another group fails the membership check" is false for global-perm holders and superusers. D1 now states the narrower property the design actually needs, and test 6 records the pre-existing behaviour instead of pretending it away.
- **Don't conflate pinning with recording** — *amended*. The original D3 rejected both on a false premise (it assumed a migration was needed). `DomainPurchase.metadata` is an existing JSONField outside both graphs, so scope + fingerprint cost nothing. D3 now records without pinning.
- **Platform-admin gate ordering sends routine tenant mistakes to the alert channel** — *amended*. The group-resolution guard now runs first (Step 5), mirroring `rest/purchase.py:132-135`.
- **Test-contamination analysis named the wrong file and mechanism** — *amended*. `4_registrar.py` is immune (`mock.patch.object` on `settings.get`); `12_config.py:72` is the exposed one. Also: testit has no teardown decorator, so delete-in-setup is the only defence.
- **`Setting.group` CASCADE is a second stale-Redis path** — *amended* into edge cases.
- **`problems` scope was underspecified** — *amended*: own scope only, never the inherited contact.
- **`is_secret` is REST masking, not encryption at rest** (`secrets.py:48-53` derives the key from the row's own non-secret columns) — *amended* into D2 and the changelog note.
- **D2's round-trip, the `mojo_secrets` graph exclusion, the queryset-delete claim, "nothing else reads this key", and route reachability/gating** — *rebutted as sound*; the challenger independently verified each and found no fault. `["SAVE_PERMS","VIEW_PERMS"]` does not union — `get_rest_meta_prop` returns the first non-None — which is what excludes `view_dns`.
